purpose: Exercise each low-byte DS:60D8 change bit immediately before the player callback and compare the 5937 dispatch path, full player record, and relevant globals.

method.command_template: python3 research/tools/quikytrace.py --launch --headless --select-level W1L1 --player-trace --player-focus-callback --player-capture-record --player-samples 1 --player-frames-between 0 --player-patch ds:0x60d8:u16=<bit> --player-patch ds:0x60da:u16=0 --player-patch ds:0x85da:u8=0 --player-watch-execute 0x1f7:0x386f --player-watch-execute 0x1f7:0x0442 --player-watch-execute 0x1f7:0x04df --player-watch-execute 0x1f7:0x0517

side_effects.direct_player_record: All eight patched runs produced the same complete 0x78-byte pre/post differences as the control; no bit-specific player simulation write was observed.
side_effects.dispatch_previous_word_60da: 5937 copies the patched DS:60D8 word into DS:60DA for every tested bit.
side_effects.dispatch_aux_4ff8: The first callback changes DS:4FF8 from 1 to 2 in both control and matrix runs; it is not bit-specific in this experiment.
side_effects.other_5937_aliases: DS:4FF2, DS:4FF6, DS:4FFA, score/lives/ammo/health, and view-state aliases showed no bit-specific change in the captured callback window.
side_effects.indirect_target: The W1L1 selector-6 record is stable at raw callback words 0000:0517 for all tested bits. The selector-5/0000:04DF record is separately observed in the natural multi-sample trace but was not entered in this one-callback matrix.

does_not_prove: side effects of table-selected callbacks in other levels or selector records
that presentation/view writes cannot affect later camera state
natural contact, ceiling, or platform behavior
next: Run the same matrix at a selector-5 state where the raw table record is 0000:04DF, then compare the shared callback frame and post-dispatch aliases.
